name: Localize
tagline: An app's translations: every string harvested from its Swift, translated by your model, checked and incremental.
description:
An app's translations, from its own Swift. Localize reads every localizable string out of the code (`Text("…")`, `Button("…")`, `.navigationTitle("…")`, `String(localized: "…")`, `NSLocalizedString`, and the properties and parameters the app declares as a `LocalizedStringKey`), with each interpolation written as the format specifier the runtime asks for: `Text("\(count) recipes")` is the key `%lld recipes`.

It writes the source language, then has the model your host has loaded translate what is new or changed into the languages you name, a batch at a time. Every answer is checked: every format specifier and line break kept, never left in English. A bad answer is asked for again with what was wrong; what still fails stays in English and is named. Say `{"languages": ["fr", "de", "ja"]}`, or `loom` for Loom's 28 languages; call again after new screens and only the new strings are asked for.

It keeps `Localizable.strings` a language or one String Catalog, adds the languages to the Xcode project's known regions, and makes sure the strings build into every app target. Without a model, it still writes the source language and says which languages wait.

One of the Rao Craft Agents: independent packages that, tagged in prompts along the life of a project, build an app of Loom's quality.
